Which explanation text should the "Which customers are your own company?" window show?
(a) The longer text, with "your location is not always a customer, and the names can differ" (suggested: it is the requirement itself and explains why nobody is preselected)
(b) The shorter text from the message table

Internal Work Orders: The estimate of a work order for the shop's own company (an internal work order)

Which stamp does an internal work order's estimate show: INTERNAL or NO CHARGE?
(a) INTERNAL on an internal work order's estimate, NO CHARGE on a customer's no-charge one, the same as the closed document (suggested)
(b) NO CHARGE on both kinds of estimate
(c) Something else (please say)

Once closed, an internal work order's document reads "Internal Work Order" with the INTERNAL stamp, and a customer's no-charge one reads "No Charge Work Order" with the NO CHARGE stamp. For the open estimate the PRD says both kinds "carry the NO CHARGE stamp". So today an internal job would say NO CHARGE on its estimate and INTERNAL on its closed document.

Internal Work Orders: The "Create invoice [number]?" window when vendor bill cost moves at invoicing

When two lines' vendor bill costs move between the same two accounts, does the window show one row or two?
(a) One row per pair of accounts, amounts added up, as the developers' plan builds it (suggested: the accounts are what the accountant reads)
(b) One row for each line or bill that moves
(c) One row per pair of accounts with the lines listed under it

When a vendor bill was posted and a line's No Charge mark changes before invoicing, Create invoice first shows a window with "Moved from [account] to [account]" rows. The PRD says one row per move. The developers' plan groups them by account pair, so two lines that both move from Cost of Parts to Warranty show as one row with the amounts added together.

Internal Work Orders: The "Closed" value in the work orders Status filter

Should a shop that has never used Internal Work Orders see "Closed" in the Status filter on the All tab?
(a) Hide "Closed" until the shop switches the setting on or closes a work order (suggested: it keeps the "no change until they turn it on" promise)

Internal Work Orders: A deposit paid on the customer portal after the work order became No Charge

Is it acceptable for v1 that this payment is refused and has to be refunded by hand?
(a) Yes for v1: the refused deposit is recorded with its own reason and the shop refunds it with the existing action (suggested: rare, and visible to the shop)
(b) No: block Convert to No Charge while a portal deposit checkout is open
(c) No: refund it automatically in this release

No Charge cannot be set while a deposit exists, and the portal refuses deposits on internal and no-charge work orders. One gap remains: the customer opens the deposit checkout on the portal while the work order is still billable, the advisor converts it to No Charge, and then the customer pays. ShopView refuses the deposit, but the card has been charged, and the money waits until someone refunds it with the existing refund action (no automatic refund in this release).
Tech plan Appendix D (lines 5237, 5298) and Appendix A (line 3116); PRD v1.0 S2-N4, S2-N5 (silent on this order of events)
Internal Work Orders: An AccountingHub account that a category row is mapped to

May we test that the hub refuses to deactivate such an account, instead of testing what happens after it is deactivated?
(a) Yes: test the refusal, and keep the "held when inactive" rule as a safety net we do not test by hand (suggested)
(b) No: the hub should allow it, then hold the entries as the PRD says

The PRD says that if a mapped account is made inactive, the hub holds the entries until the row is changed. In AccountingHub today an account that any mapping row points at cannot be deactivated, and the developers add the category rows to that check, so the inactive state can only happen through a database change.
PRD v1.0 S6-E1; tech plan Appendix C (lines 3884, 4183)
Internal Work Orders: No-charge lines after converting the whole work order to No Charge and back

After a work order with Warranty or Comeback lines is converted to No Charge and later back to billable, should those lines get their own marks back?
(a) Every line comes back billable; the advisor marks lines again if needed (suggested: matches "Every line is priced as a new line would be today.")
(b) Lines that had their own No Charge mark before get it back with their category

Converting the whole work order to No Charge puts every line under the work order's category and replaces the lines' own categories. The developers' plan clears the lines' own marks at that point, so after Convert to Billable every line comes back as an ordinary billable line and the advisor marks them again if needed.
PRD v1.0 S2-R5, S2-R6; tech plan Appendix A (line 2385)

Internal Work Orders: The Comeback rate in the Internal Work Orders report, By technician tab

What should the rate show for a technician who has comebacks but no completed lines in the chosen dates?
(a) A dash or an empty cell, not a number (suggested: 0% and 100% would both mislead)
(b) 0%
(c) Something else (please say)
The rate is comeback lines divided by completed lines. When a comeback lands in a month in which the original technician completed nothing (or has left), that division has nothing to divide by.

Questions from reading the design (12 Nov 2026), questions 12 to 16
Internal Work Orders: The helper texts for categories on the Internal Work Orders page and on Edit Customer

What should the category helper texts say, now that the category is never changed on the work order?
(a) Texts that match the PRD, for example "It shows on the NO CHARGE document and the Internal Work Orders report." and no "a work order can change it" (suggested: the behaviour is already settled, only the words are missing)
(b) The design's texts as drawn
(c) No helper text in these places

The design's texts say the category shows on, and can be changed on, the work order: the New No Charge Category window says "It shows on the work order, the NO CHARGE document and the Internal Work Orders report.", the Internal categories tab says "a work order can change it", and Edit Customer says the default category is "Preselected on every new work order for this customer; a work order can change it." The PRD says the opposite on both points: the category is not shown on the work order (only the badge is), and an internal work order's category is changed on the asset or the customer, never on the work order. The PRD gives no wording for these helper lines, so we cannot check them yet. The rest of each screen is tested now.
